newsitem.title: UK: London gold holds levels in quiet holiday market.
newsitem.headline: London gold holds levels in quiet holiday market.

text.p: Interest in gold was subdued on Thursday afternoon after New York opened quietly to continue the light volumes seen earlier in Europe.
The May Day holiday in most of Europe and Golden Week holidays in Japan kept business at low levels, but dealers said expectations were for recent losses to continue.
Bullion fixed 30 cents easier at $339.25 from the morning level, which in turn was 60 cents below Thursday afternoon.
Feelings toward gold remained overwhelmingly bearish with fears of future central bank sales keeping bullion's prospects strictly capped under $350.00, dealers said.
The rush by the dollar to multi-year highs earlier this week had put pressure on gold, and even its drift down in light holiday forex markets did not stimulate interest in bullion.
There was little reaction to U.S. jobless claims for the week ending April 26 coming out at 347,000 from a revised 319,000 the previous week.
A brief slip to around $338.60 found support with a one-dollar bounce, leading dealers to see the possibility of a crawl back over $340.00.
"It bounced from the $338-$339 level every time it got there. I think it might be edging its way back above $340 today," said one London dealer.

The next significant U.S. figure will be unemployment, which the market will examine for clues on the likelihood of U.S. rate hikes. Friday's key non-farm payroll data are forecast for an unchanged 5.2 percent.
The most likely time for a hike in U.S. interest rates would be May 20 after the policy advising Federal Open Markets Committee meeting.
Most technical analysts maintain a bearish stance on gold while a downtrend line extending from $363.95 remained in place.
On the upside, resistance was heavy at $342.50 then $345.00.
Platinum forward rates softened early with one-month leasing quoted at eight percent from 9-10 previously.
"Somebody has lent the metal out," said one dealer.
But last month's activity on protracted delays in Russian supplies was receding. "These stories are getting a bit stale after a while," the dealer added.
Spot platinum was quoted 40 cents higher at $372.00/$373.00, while palladium shed $0.25 to $156.00/$157.00.
Silver stood three cents down at $4.67/$4.69 and its potential gains were seen limited to $4.73 for now.
